You do not need to change your name. You do not need to tell anyone today. Take a full wash when you can, which is recommended for someone who has just become Muslim, and then learn wudu and the prayer — in that order, without rushing.

Fasting in Ramadan
No food, drink or intimacy from dawn until sunset, for the month of Ramadan.

Ramadan moves through the year, so its length and difficulty change with the season. There are real exemptions — illness, travel, pregnancy, nursing, menstruation, old age — and taking one is not a failure. Some days are made up later, some are not.
Obligatory charity
A yearly share of the wealth you have held onto, given to those entitled to it.

Zakat is not a donation you choose to make — it is a portion of your savings that stops being yours. It applies only above a threshold, and only to wealth you have held for a full lunar year, so many people newly earning owe none at all. Whether it applies to you is worth asking someone locally rather than working out alone.
Pilgrimage
The pilgrimage to Mecca, once in a lifetime, for those able to make it.

Hajj happens on fixed days of the Islamic year and is required once, and only if you can afford it and are physically able. Most Muslims go later in life, if at all. Nothing about it is expected of you now.
Prayer
Five prayers a day, at set times, facing the Kaʿbah in Mecca.

Fajr before sunrise, Dhuhr after midday, ʿAsr in the afternoon, Maghrib just after sunset, and ʿIshaʾ at night. Each one takes a few minutes. You wash first — that is wudu — and the app walks you through both.

Rinse your mouth
Take water into your mouth with your right hand, swill it around and spit it out. Three times.
Rinse your nose
Sniff a little water into your nose with your right hand, then blow it out using your left. Three times.
Wash your arms
Wash your right arm from the fingertips to just past the elbow, three times. Then the left, three times.
Right before left is the pattern for everything that comes in a pair.
Wash your face
Wash your whole face three times — from your hairline to under your chin, and from ear to ear.
Wash your feet
Wash your right foot to just past the ankle, between the toes, three times. Then the left, three times.
Wash your hands
Wash both hands up to the wrists, three times, between the fingers.
Wipe your ears
With the same wetness, put your index fingers inside your ears and your thumbs behind them, and wipe. Once.
Wipe your head
With wet hands, wipe over your head from the front to the back and return to the front. Once.
Wiping, not washing — and once, not three times.
